The 1-month estimate extends that drift further, incorporating a slightly more optimistic view that any near-term consolidation resolves to the upside, perhaps driven by sector tailwinds or improving fundamentals over a longer horizon.

By the 1-week horizon, the band widens to nearly two points in each direction, accounting for the possibility of earnings surprises, macroeconomic data releases, or shifts in sector sentiment. Macro shocks — such as a sudden credit event, a surprise inflation print, or a geopolitical escalation — represent tail risks that my intervals do not fully capture, since they are by construction 90% confidence intervals, meaning roughly one in ten outcomes should fall outside them under my model assumptions.

Finally, I want to be transparent that these estimates carry meaningful model uncertainty on top of market uncertainty.
